extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in journalism ethics, newsroom editors, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and observed practices related to verifying sources, handling allegations of fabricated quotes, and newsroom corrective actions (amendments vs retractions) illustrated by a journalist's case. Useful for evaluating source reliability and editorial responses in news reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability of secondary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of Delio's 'secondary' sources (i.e., those added for color or supporting quotes) were unverifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary sources used to provide color or supporting quotes must be verifiable; an internal review found unverifiable secondary sources which led to amendments of articles (Wired amended 24 articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability of primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Her 'primary' sources (i.e., those most essential to her stories) were legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize verification of primary sources because they are essential to a story's substance; if primary sources are reliable, the core claims may remain valid even if peripheral sourcing has issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and scrutiny of anonymous sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The incident began when Delio published an article ... based on an interview with 'G.S', an anonymous insider at Hewlett-Packard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims based on anonymous insiders require heightened scrutiny and corroboration; challenges from the subject (e.g., a corporation) can trigger editorial review and potential retraction if not sufficiently supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of fabricated 'color quotes'
rubrics_metrics.description: It was alleged that Delio had made up 'color quotes' for some of her articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabricating quotes or inventing supporting details is a serious ethical breach that undermines credibility and can prompt corrections, amendments, or full retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate editorial corrective actions (amendment vs retraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: MIT Technology Review retracted the article. Wired News amended 24 of Delio's articles, while MIT Technology Review retracted 10 completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should choose corrective action based on severity and impact: amend articles when peripheral elements are faulty but core substance stands; retract when key claims or essential sourcing are unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal review/audit of past reporting after allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Wired News conducted an internal study ... Of 160 stories reviewed, 24 had problems with at least one source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allegations arise, conduct a comprehensive internal audit of past reporting to assess scope and identify problematic items requiring correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of impact on article substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Of 160 stories reviewed, 24 had problems with at least one source, although no evidence was forthcoming to suggest the main substance of the articles was skewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether source issues affect the article's main substance; if the core reporting is unchanged, corrections may suffice instead of retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in reporting investigations and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Wired News released a source review and amended stories; MIT Technology Review issued retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly disclose the results of investigations and any corrections or retractions to maintain accountability and public trust.
